Let's introduce the new variable $u=4-{x}^{4}.$ Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-4{x}^{3}\,⟹\,-2\text{d}u=8{x}^{3}\text{d}x.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 8{x}^{3}{e}^{4-{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x & =\int {e}^{4-{x}^{4}}\cdot 8{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int {e}^{u}\cdot (-2)\,\text{d}u \\  & =-2\int {e}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-2{e}^{u}+C \\  & =-2{e}^{4-{x}^{4}}+C.\end{aligned}
$$
